title_en: Li Min v. Zhu Jinhua, Li Shaohua — dispute over reward for a public reward advertisement (appeal)
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over reward advertisement; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Tianjin; Natural person; General Principles of the Civil Law; Validity of reward advertisement; True expression of intention; Principle of good faith; Partial support; Lost briefcase; Reward advertisement; Finder's claim for reward; Good faith; Li Shaohua reward advertisement reward dispute
full_text_en:
Li Min v. Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua — Dispute over Reward for Lost Property (Appeal)

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): Li Min, female, 34 years old, worker at Tianjin Municipal Engineering Bureau.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance): Zhu Jinhua, male, 37 years old, worker at Tianjin Locomotive and Rolling Stock Parts Factory, Beijing Railway Bureau.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance): Li Shaohua, male, 32 years old, cadre at Luoyang Electromechanical Company, Henan Province.

Third party at first instance: Wang Jiaping, male, 35 years old, police officer at Heping Branch of Tianjin Public Security Bureau.

The appellant Li Min, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (1993) He Min Chu Zi No. 440 rendered by the Heping District People's Court of Tianjin in the case of dispute over reward for lost property against the respondents Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua, appealed to the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court.

The court of first instance found the following facts: The respondent Zhu Jinhua and the respondent Li Shaohua were friends. Li Shaohua entrusted Zhu Jinhua to handle the vehicle delivery procedures. At noon on March 30, 1993, while watching a movie at the Heping District Cinema in Tianjin, Zhu Jinhua left a briefcase containing automobile delivery orders and related fee documents with a face value of over RMB 800,000 from the Luoyang Electromechanical Company on his seat after the movie ended. The appellant Li Min, who was watching the movie several rows behind, discovered the briefcase and picked it up. Together with the third party Wang Jiaping (a former classmate of Li Min) who had accompanied her to the movie, she waited at the scene for a considerable time but did not see the owner come to look for it. She then took the briefcase away and entrusted Wang Jiaping with its safekeeping. On April 4, 5, and 7 of the same year, Zhu Jinhua successively published lost-and-found notices in the Tianjin *Jinwan Bao* (Tonight News) and *Tianjin Daily*, indicating that he would "generously reward" or "must generously reward" the finder. On April 12, after learning of the loss, Li Shaohua published a lost-and-found notice with identical content in the *Jinwan Bao*, stating: "A reward of RMB 15,000 will be given to anyone who returns the item within one week." That evening, after Li Min learned of the notice published in Li Shaohua's name, she immediately informed Wang Jiaping and asked him to contact Li Shaohua. On the following day, the parties exchanged the money and items at the agreed time and place. A dispute arose over the payment of the reward, and Li Min subsequently filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting that Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua pay the promised reward of RMB 15,000. Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua argued that the promise to pay a reward in the lost-and-found notice was not their true intention, and that the briefcase contained contact information for Li Shaohua and his work unit; Li Min failed to proactively seek out the owner to return the property, instead waiting for a reward, and thus requested the court to dismiss Li Min's claims. Wang Jiaping stated that he was merely keeping the briefcase for Li Min and did not claim any reward. The court of first instance held that the briefcase containing the automobile delivery orders and fee documents with a face value of over RMB 800,000, which Li Min had picked up at the cinema, was indeed the property of the respondent Li Shaohua's work unit and had been lost by the respondent Zhu Jinhua. Based on the delivery orders and other items inside the briefcase, the loser or the owner's work unit could be identified. In accordance with Article 79, paragraph 2 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC*, Li Min should have returned the lost property to the owner. However, Li Min did not proactively contact the loser but instead stayed home waiting for the reward promised in the lost-and-found notice, which was not a genuine expression of intention. According to Article 58, item (3) of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, a civil act performed under circumstances where the true intention is contradicted shall be void. The court did not support Li Min's claim. Accordingly, on June 16, 1994, the court rendered the following judgment: Li Min's claim was dismissed. The court costs of RMB 625 were borne by Li Min.

Li Min, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court on the ground that the court below had incorrectly applied the law.

Upon trial, the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court found that the facts determined by the court of first instance were clear, but the court below had insufficient basis for concluding that the respondents Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua were not expressing their true intention when promising a reward in the lost-and-found notices. A reward advertisement is an act by which the advertiser, through an advertisement, promises to pay a reward to a person who performs a specified act. As long as the actor lawfully completes the designated act, the advertiser is obligated to pay the reward. The lost-and-found notices successively published by Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua in the Tianjin *Jinwan Bao* and *Tianjin Daily* constituted reward advertisements. Li Shaohua further explicitly stated: "A reward of RMB 15,000 will be given to anyone who returns the item within one week." This was an offer made to unspecified persons in society. The appellant Li Min, as the actor in the reward advertisement, performed the act specified in the advertisement (returning the briefcase) within the "one week" period stipulated in the advertisement, thus constituting an effective acceptance of the offer. Consequently, a civil legal relationship, namely a creditor-debt relationship, was formed between Li Min and Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua. In accordance with Article 57 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, which provides that "a civil juristic act shall be legally binding from the time of its establishment. Unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the other party, the actor shall not alter or rescind the act without authorization," Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua were obligated to pay the reward as promised in the advertisement. Their argument that the promise to pay a reward in the lost-and-found notice was not their true intention, and their subsequent retraction and refusal to pay Li Min the RMB 15,000 reward, violated the principle of good faith provided for in Article 4 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law* and were erroneous. The grounds of Li Min's appeal were well-founded and should be supported. The first-instance judgment was improper and should be corrected.

In accordance with Article 85 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, on the basis of clear facts and after distinguishing right from wrong, the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court conducted mediation, and on December 26, 1994, both parties voluntarily reached the following agreement:

Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua shall pay Li Min a reward of RMB 8,000 in a lump sum.

Court costs for the first and second instances totaling RMB 1,435 shall be borne by Li Min in the amount of RMB 635 and by Zhu Jinhua and Li Shaohua in the amount of RMB 800.
